There are two opinions concerning it.

The first: it is Medinan. This was related by Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas, and Qatadah and others held this view.

The second: it is Meccan. This was related by Kurayb from Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan, Ata', Ikrimah and Jabir held this view. The first is more sound, and it is supported by the report that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was bewitched while he was with Aisha, and then the two protective surahs (al-Mu'awwidhatan) were revealed to him."

The people of tafsir (exegesis) mentioned concerning their revelation: "A boy from among the Jews used to serve the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Jews kept at him until he took a comb of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) hair and a number of teeth from his comb, and gave them to the Jews, and they cast a spell upon him with them. The one who undertook this was Labid ibn al-A'sam, the Jew. Then he placed them in a well belonging to the Banu Zurayq, called the Well of Dharwan. It is also said: Dhi Arwan. (p-271) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell ill, and the hair of his head fell out. He would think that he had come to his wives when he had not come to them, and it would be imagined to him that he was doing something when he was not doing it. Then one day, while he was asleep, two angels came to him; one sat at his head and the other at his feet. One of them said to the other: 'What is the matter with the man?' The other said: 'He has been bewitched.' He said: 'And who bewitched him?' He said: 'Labid ibn al-A'sam.' He said: 'With what did he bewitch him?' He said: 'With a comb and combings.' He said: 'And where is it?' He said: 'In the sheath of a date-spathe, under a rā'ūfah in the Well of Dharwan.' (Al-juff: the skin of the date-spathe. Al-rā'ūfah: a rock left at the bottom of a well when it is dug; when they wish to clean the well, the one cleaning it sits upon it.) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) awoke and said: 'O Aisha, did you not realize that Allah informed me of my illness? Then He sent Ali, al-Zubayr and Ammar ibn Yasir, and they drained the water of that well, then they lifted the rock and brought out the sheath, and in it were the combings of his head and the teeth of his comb, and a cord tied with eleven knots [stuck with a needle; then Allah the Exalted sent down the two surahs, and every time he recited a verse, a knot came undone]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) felt relief when the last knot came undone. Jibril (peace be upon him) began to say: "In the name of Allah, I perform ruqyah for you from everything that harms you, and from an envier and an evil eye, and Allah will heal you." They said: "O Messenger of Allah (p-272) shall we not take the evil one and kill him?" He said: "As for me, Allah has healed me, and I dislike stirring up evil among the people."'"

Al-Bukhari and Muslim in their two Sahihs have related from the hadith of Aisha the hadith of the bewitchment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). We have already explained the meaning of ﴿a'udhu﴾ at the beginning of our book.

The first: it is the dawn. This was related by al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Qurazi and Ibn Zayd held this view. The linguists said: it is said, "This is clearer than the splitting (falaq) of dawn and the cleaving (faraq) of dawn."

(p-273) The second: it is the creation. This was related by al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas. Likewise al-Dahhak said: al-falaq is all of creation.

The third: it is a prison in Hell. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas as well. Wahb and al-Suddi said: it is a pit in Hell. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: it is a valley in Hell.

The fourth: it is a tree in the Fire. This was said by Abdullah ibn Amr.

The fifth: it is everything that splits open, such as dawn, a grain, a date-stone, and other things. This was said by al-Hasan. Al-Zajjaj said: If you reflect upon creation, it becomes clear to you that most of it comes from splitting, like the earth with plants, and the cloud with rain.

The sixth: it is a name of Hell. This was said by Abu Abd al-Rahman Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Habli.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿from the evil of what He created﴾. Ibn al-Samayfa' and Ibn Ya'mar read "khuliqa" with a damma on the kha and a kasra on the lam. Concerning this there are three opinions.

The first: it is general, and this is the most apparent.

The second: the evil of what is created is Iblis and his offspring; this was said by al-Hasan.

The third: it is Hell; this was related by al-Mawardi.

(p-274) Concerning ﴿al-ghasiq﴾ there are four opinions.

The first: it is the moon. Aisha related: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at the moon and said: 'Seek refuge in Allah from its evil, for it is al-ghasiq when it wanes (idha waqab).'" This was related by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in their books. Ibn Qutaybah said: it is also said: al-ghasiq is the moon when it eclipses and darkens. The meaning of "waqab" is that it enters into eclipse.

The second: it is the star. This was related from Abu Hurayrah from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The third: it is the night. This was said by Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Qurazi, al-Farra', Abu Ubayd, Ibn Qutaybah and al-Zajjaj. The linguists said: the meaning of ﴿waqab﴾ is that it enters into everything and so darkens it. And "al-ghasaq" is darkness. Al-Zajjaj said: al-ghasiq means the cold; the night is called ghasiq because it is colder than the day.

The fourth: it is the Pleiades when they set, and when they set plagues and diseases become frequent (p-275) at their setting and are lifted at their rising; this was said by Ibn Zayd.

Al-Zajjaj said: they spit without saliva, as if it were a puff of breath. Ibn al-Anbari said: the linguists said: the explanation of "nafatha" is to blow without saliva, and the meaning of "tafala" is to blow with saliva. Dhu al-Rummah said:

The fourth: it is the Pleiades when they set, and when they set plagues and diseases become frequent (p-275) at their setting and are lifted at their rising; this was said by Ibn Zayd.

As for ﴿al-naffathat﴾, Ibn Qutaybah said: they are the sorceresses who blow (yanfuthna), that is, they spit when they cast spells and recite incantations. Al-Zajjaj said: they spit without saliva, as if it were a puff of breath. Ibn al-Anbari said: the linguists said: the explanation of "nafatha" is to blow without saliva, and the meaning of "tafala" is to blow with saliva. Dhu al-Rummah said:

"And from the midst of water, its surface green with moss, when the water-drawer of the people touches it, it spits (yatfulu)."

Ibn Abi Suraij related "al-nafithat" with an alif before the fa', with the fa' kasra and light.

Some of the exegetes said: what is meant here by al-naffathat is the daughters of Labid ibn al-A'sam the Jew, who bewitched the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

(p-276) ﴿And from the evil of the envier﴾, that is, the Jews envied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). We have mentioned the limit of envy under [al-Baqarah: 109]. Envy is the basest of dispositions. The first disobedience by which Allah was disobeyed in the heavens was the envy of Iblis toward Adam, and on earth the envy of Qabil toward Habil.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 113, verse 1–5:

(p-270) Surat al-Falaq

There are two opinions concerning it.

The first: it is Medinan. This was related by Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas, and Qatadah and others held this view.

The second: it is Meccan. This was related by Kurayb from Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan, Ata', Ikrimah and Jabir held this view. The first is more sound, and it is supported by the report that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was bewitched while he was with Aisha, and then the two protective surahs (al-Mu'awwidhatan) were revealed to him."

The people of tafsir (exegesis) mentioned concerning their revelation: "A boy from among the Jews used to serve the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Jews kept at him until he took a comb of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) hair and a number of teeth from his comb, and gave them to the Jews, and they cast a spell upon him with them. The one who undertook this was Labid ibn al-A'sam, the Jew. Then he placed them in a well belonging to the Banu Zurayq, called the Well of Dharwan. It is also said: Dhi Arwan. (p-271) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell ill, and the hair of his head fell out. He would think that he had come to his wives when he had not come to them, and it would be imagined to him that he was doing something when he was not doing it. Then one day, while he was asleep, two angels came to him; one sat at his head and the other at his feet. One of them said to the other: 'What is the matter with the man?' The other said: 'He has been bewitched.' He said: 'And who bewitched him?' He said: 'Labid ibn al-A'sam.' He said: 'With what did he bewitch him?' He said: 'With a comb and combings.' He said: 'And where is it?' He said: 'In the sheath of a date-spathe, under a rā'ūfah in the Well of Dharwan.' (Al-juff: the skin of the date-spathe. Al-rā'ūfah: a rock left at the bottom of a well when it is dug; when they wish to clean the well, the one cleaning it sits upon it.) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) awoke and said: 'O Aisha, did you not realize that Allah informed me of my illness? Then He sent Ali, al-Zubayr and Ammar ibn Yasir, and they drained the water of that well, then they lifted the rock and brought out the sheath, and in it were the combings of his head and the teeth of his comb, and a cord tied with eleven knots [stuck with a needle; then Allah the Exalted sent down the two surahs, and every time he recited a verse, a knot came undone]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) felt relief when the last knot came undone. Jibril (peace be upon him) began to say: "In the name of Allah, I perform ruqyah for you from everything that harms you, and from an envier and an evil eye, and Allah will heal you." They said: "O Messenger of Allah (p-272) shall we not take the evil one and kill him?" He said: "As for me, Allah has healed me, and I dislike stirring up evil among the people."'"

Al-Bukhari and Muslim in their two Sahihs have related from the hadith of Aisha the hadith of the bewitchment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). We have already explained the meaning of ﴿a'udhu﴾ at the beginning of our book.

Concerning ﴿al-falaq﴾ there are six opinions.

The first: it is the dawn. This was related by al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Qurazi and Ibn Zayd held this view. The linguists said: it is said, "This is clearer than the splitting (falaq) of dawn and the cleaving (faraq) of dawn."

(p-273) The second: it is the creation. This was related by al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas. Likewise al-Dahhak said: al-falaq is all of creation.

The third: it is a prison in Hell. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas as well. Wahb and al-Suddi said: it is a pit in Hell. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: it is a valley in Hell.

The fourth: it is a tree in the Fire. This was said by Abdullah ibn Amr.

The fifth: it is everything that splits open, such as dawn, a grain, a date-stone, and other things. This was said by al-Hasan. Al-Zajjaj said: If you reflect upon creation, it becomes clear to you that most of it comes from splitting, like the earth with plants, and the cloud with rain.

The sixth: it is a name of Hell. This was said by Abu Abd al-Rahman Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Habli.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿from the evil of what He created﴾. Ibn al-Samayfa' and Ibn Ya'mar read "khuliqa" with a damma on the kha and a kasra on the lam. Concerning this there are three opinions.

The first: it is general, and this is the most apparent.

The second: the evil of what is created is Iblis and his offspring; this was said by al-Hasan.

The third: it is Hell; this was related by al-Mawardi.

(p-274) Concerning ﴿al-ghasiq﴾ there are four opinions.

The first: it is the moon. Aisha related: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at the moon and said: 'Seek refuge in Allah from its evil, for it is al-ghasiq when it wanes (idha waqab).'" This was related by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in their books. Ibn Qutaybah said: it is also said: al-ghasiq is the moon when it eclipses and darkens. The meaning of "waqab" is that it enters into eclipse.

The second: it is the star. This was related from Abu Hurayrah from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The third: it is the night. This was said by Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Qurazi, al-Farra', Abu Ubayd, Ibn Qutaybah and al-Zajjaj. The linguists said: the meaning of ﴿waqab﴾ is that it enters into everything and so darkens it. And "al-ghasaq" is darkness. Al-Zajjaj said: al-ghasiq means the cold; the night is called ghasiq because it is colder than the day.
